title: Nasruddin and Timur
summary: Timur the Conqueror looked into a mirror, saw his scarred face and blind eye, and burst into tears of grief. His courtiers immediately began weeping in sycophantic sympathy....
full_text:
Timur the Conqueror looked into a mirror, saw his scarred face and blind eye, and burst into tears of grief. His courtiers immediately began weeping in sycophantic sympathy.

After two hours, Timur stopped weeping and smiled, and his courtiers instantly dried their eyes. Only Mulla Nasruddin continued to wail at the top of his lungs, tearing his robe.

"Mulla," snapped Timur, "I have stopped weeping; why do you continue to howl?"

"Sire!" sobbed Nasruddin. "You looked into the mirror for a single minute and wept for two hours. I have to look at your face all day long; imagine how much more I must weep!" Timur burst into laughter and rewarded the fearless Mulla.
moral: Clever wit and unflinching presence of mind can disarm even the most ruthless tyrant.
